### I Am the Good Shepherd - The Crosswalk Devotional - September 19
Author: Emma Danzey
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-devo/i-am-the-good-shepherd-the-crosswalk-devotional.html
Passage: John 10:11
Points:
- Jesus demonstrated the depth of His sacrificial love by laying down His life for His sheep.
- Believers are spiritually helpless on their own and must acknowledge their total dependence on the Shepherd.
- Christ does not see believers as nameless faces in a crowd, but knows and cherishes each person individually.
- God's people must guard against deceptive voices by staying rooted in the voice of Jesus found in Scripture.
- Following the Good Shepherd leads through paths of righteousness and spiritual blessing rather than easy worldly paths.

### 3 Comforts Christians Can Draw from the Good Shepherd in John 10
Author: Aaron D'Anthony Brown
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/faith/spiritual-life/who-is-the-good-shepherd-in-john-10.html
Passage: John 10:11
Points:
- Unlike a hired worker who flees in danger, Jesus showed supreme devotion by dying for His flock.
- Human beings are spiritually vulnerable and require the constant protection of Christ against the enemy.
- Believers belong to God and can find assurance knowing they are deeply valued and cared for.
- The Good Shepherd provides both physical and spiritual sustenance, supplying everything His people truly need.
- God never tires of being with His sheep, faithfully guiding them with patience through every season.

### Are You Missing Out on the Abundant Life that Jesus Talked About?
Author: Tim Pietz
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/faith/spiritual-life/are-you-missing-out-on-the-abundant-life-that-jesus-talked-about.html
Passage: John 10:10
Points:
- Jesus fulfills the prophetic promise of Ezekiel 34 as the true Shepherd in contrast to destructive, self-serving leaders.
- The Pharisees turned religion into a transactional system of legalism and missed the heart of God.
- True abundance is not defined by worldly power, wealth, or comfort, but by humble obedience and loving servanthood.
- Real obedience flows from loving God and neighbor rather than keeping external rules to earn favor.
- Abundant life is found primarily in an intimate, ongoing relationship with the Good Shepherd Himself.
